## Statute

Section 7703(a)(2) (line 510): "an individual legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married."

Section 2(b)(1) (line 204): "An individual shall be considered a head of a household if, and only if, such individual is not married at the close of his taxable year, is not a surviving spouse (as defined in subsection (a)), and either-(A) maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of such taxable year the principal place of abode, as a member of such household, of-(i) a qualifying child of the individual (as defined in section 152(c)), but not if such child-(I) is married at the close of the taxpayer's taxable year, and (II) is not a dependent of such individual by reason of section 152(b)(2)"

Section 152(c)(1) (line 110): "The term 'qualifying child' means, with respect to any taxpayer for any taxable year, an individual-(A) who bears a relationship to the taxpayer described in paragraph (2), (B) who has the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than one-half of such taxable year, (C) who meets the age requirements of paragraph (3), and (E) who has not filed a joint return (other than only for a claim of refund) with the individual's spouse for the taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins."

Section 152(c)(2)(A) (line 119): "an individual bears a relationship to the taxpayer described in this paragraph if such individual is-(A) a child of the taxpayer or a descendant of such a child"

Section 152(c)(3) (line 127): "an individual meets the requirements of this paragraph if such individual is younger than the taxpayer claiming such individual as a qualifying child and is less than 25 years old at the end of the taxable year."

Section 63(c)(2)(B) (line 394): "the basic standard deduction is-(B) $4,400 in the case of a head of household (as defined in section 2(b))"

Section 151(c) (line 64): "An exemption of the exemption amount for each individual who is a dependent (as defined in section 152) of the taxpayer for the taxable year."

Section 151(d)(1) (line 70): "the term 'exemption amount' means $2,000."

Section 1(b)(i) (line 23): "15% of taxable income if the taxable income is not over $29,600"

## Reasoning

1. Filing Status: Alice was legally separated under a decree of divorce on March 2nd, 2015 (§7703(a)(2), line 510). Therefore, she is "not married" for tax purposes in 2017.

2. Head of Household: Alice qualifies as head of household under §2(b)(1), line 204 because:
   - She is not married (divorced in 2015)
   - Charlie is her qualifying child
   - Charlie is her child (§152(c)(2)(A), line 119)
   - Charlie has the same principal place of abode as Alice for more than half the year ("Alice and Charlie live in a house maintained by Alice")
   - Charlie is 5 years old in 2017 (born Feb 2, 2012), meeting the age requirement of <25 years (§152(c)(3), line 127)
   - Charlie has not filed a joint return

3. Standard Deduction: As a head of household, Alice's basic standard deduction is $4,400 (§63(c)(2)(B), line 394).

4. Personal Exemptions: Alice gets:
   - $2,000 for herself (§151(d)(1), line 70)
   - $2,000 for Charlie as a dependent (§151(c), line 64; §151(d)(1), line 70)
   - Total exemptions: $4,000

5. Taxable Income Computation:
   - Gross income: $9,560 (given fact)
   - Less standard deduction: $4,400 (§63(c)(2)(B), line 394)
   - Less exemptions: $4,000 (§151(c), line 64; §151(d)(1), line 70)
   - Taxable income = $9,560 - $4,400 - $4,000 = $1,160

6. Tax Calculation:
   - Taxable income of $1,160 is not over $29,600
   - Tax rate: 15% (§1(b)(i), line 23)
   - Tax = 15% × $1,160 = $174

## Answer
Answer: 174
